title: The Summer of Junebug Creek
premise: Cellist Lena Quintana, whose hands froze mid-concert in a catastrophic final performance, retreats to Junebug Creek to settle her late grandmother's orchard—only to find the deed lists a co-owner: Eli Marchand, the boy who left her fifteen years ago and now returns as the lawyer representing the development company trying to buy the land. As Lena and Eli are forced to work the orchard together to satisfy an old inheritance clause, she uncovers proof that the town's beloved judge orchestrated the development deal and framed her grandmother for the debt. Choosing justice outside the law over the settlement money, Lena and Eli expose the judge at a harvest festival, and Lena, playing her cello for the town she'd fled, discovers that forgiveness—of Eli, and of the woman in the mirror—was the second chance she'd been waiting for all along.
about_author: Sebastian Joubert is the pen name of a former orchard worker from the Gulf South who spent a decade writing legal briefs before turning to fiction. His novels blend small-town heat, tangled inheritances, and love stories that cost their characters something real.

chapters.title: The Broken String
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A flashback-tinged opening: mid-symphony, Lena's hands fail, the hall goes silent, and her career dies in ninety seconds of public humiliation. Six months later she arrives at Junebug Creek to settle her grandmother's estate, carrying her cello like contraband. Emotional beat: shame disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the county clerk's office, Lena discovers the deed names a co-inheritor: Eli Marchand. Her fury is interrupted by a developer's letter offering a fortune for the orchard, contingent on both heirs agreeing. Emotional beat: the past arriving with paperwork.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli returns to town as counsel for the development firm, telling himself the orchard is just a closing. Seeing Lena on the porch, cello case at her feet, undoes fifteen years of careful distance. Emotional beat: guilt wearing a pressed suit.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Buried in grandmother Ruth's will: the orchard cannot be sold unless both heirs work it together through one full harvest season. Lena's lawyer warns the clause is airtight—Ruth planned it that way. Emotional beat: a dead woman's chess move.

chapters.title: Junebugs at Dusk
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First forced day of shared labor; they fight about everything except the real thing. When the Junebugs rise at dusk, an old tenderness flickers and both retreat from it. Emotional beat: muscle memory of love.

chapters.title: The Judge's Favor
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Judge Hollis Whitcomb, town patriarch, offers Lena a generous personal settlement if she'll persuade Eli to sell. His kindness has teeth, and Lena, desperate to leave her failure behind, almost takes it. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Ruth Kept
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. In the orchard shed, Eli finds Ruth's ledgers showing the orchard was solvent—until a debt appeared that makes no sense. He begins quietly pulling records, torn between his employer and the truth. Emotional beat: a lawyer discovering a conscience.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A storm traps them in the barn; Lena plays for the first time since the collapse, badly, and Eli doesn't flinch. They speak honestly about the night he left—his family's ruin, his silence, her abandonment. Emotional beat: the thaw.

chapters.title: The Water Bill
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Eli traces the fake debt to a shell company connected to Whitcomb's development partners. Meanwhile Lena notices the town's water rights quietly transferred to the same entity. Emotional beat: the plot widens.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Terms
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli offers Lena a secret: he'll walk away from the firm and fight the sale if she'll trust him again. She refuses—she can't afford another betrayal, and she doesn't trust her own judgment. Emotional beat: love offered, duty refused.

chapters.title: The Mirror in the Music Room
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena finds Ruth's old music room and a letter Ruth never sent, confessing her own lifelong fear of performing after one failure. Lena realizes her grandmother's clause wasn't about the orchard at all. Emotional beat: forgiving the person in the mirror begins.

chapters.title: Intimidation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Whitcomb's men damage irrigation lines and threaten the orchard hands; a fire nearly takes the packing shed. The couple realizes the deadline isn't just seasonal—someone wants them gone before harvest. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The County Records Room
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. A midnight dig through county archives yields the forged signature on the original debt. Eli photographs everything, knowing his firm will disbar him if caught. Emotional beat: crossing the line from lawyer to conspirator.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena canvasses old-timers and finds a farmhand who saw Whitcomb coerce Ruth into signing. But he's frightened, and Whitcomb's reach touches the sheriff's office. Emotional beat: justice needs witnesses, and witnesses need courage.

chapters.title: The Offer She Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Whitcomb, aware of their digging, threatens Lena with an old charge against her grandmother—and offers to make her career-ruining performance vanish from the record if she sells. Emotional beat: power corrupting, explicitly.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Shape
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli's firm discovers his leaks; his mentor offers him partnership if he hands over the evidence. Alone at night, Eli nearly does it—then burns the offer. Emotional beat: the corruption he fled has followed him inside.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The season's work is done; the clause is satisfied and the sale can legally proceed. Lena and Eli, exhausted and changed, finally admit they love each other—and that love may not be enough to save the orchard. Emotional beat: tenderness on the edge of loss.

chapters.title: The Festival
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax, part one: at the harvest festival, before the whole town and Whitcomb himself, Lena takes the stage with her cello—the instrument that ruined her—and plays. Her hands hold. Then she tells the town about the deed, the debt, and the judge. Emotional beat: the performance that redeems the first one.

chapters.title: Evidence in the Open
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Climax, part two: Eli presents the forged documents publicly, and the frightened farmhand steps forward to testify. Whitcomb's allies scatter; the sheriff, freed from the judge's shadow, takes the file. Emotional beat: justice outside the courtroom.

chapters.title: After the Fall
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Fallout: Whitcomb indicted, the development dead, the orchard legally theirs—but Eli, disbarred and stripped, assumes he must leave again. Lena, who once fled from failure, refuses to let him. Emotional beat: love choosing to stay.

chapters.title: The Second Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: the orchard in bloom, Eli teaching himself farm law as an advocate for smallholders, Lena accepting a teaching post and a local concert series. They replant what was damaged, together. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy.

chapters.title: Junebug Creek, Rising
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. One year on, at the festival's second night, Lena performs a piece she composed for Ruth, with Eli in the front row. The Junebugs rise; the town sings along off-key; nothing is broken. Final line lands on the deed, reframed on the wall: two names, one orchard, no conditions. Emotional beat: second chances, kept.
